research.facts:
Kawhi Leonard — Second Secret Endorsement Deal Exposed (Daktronics)
**Sources searched:** NBC Sports, CBS Sports, HoopsHype, ESPN, NBA.com, Yahoo Sports
**Verified facts (CONFIDENCE LEVELS):**
- HIGH: NBA investigation into Kawhi Leonard trade to Toronto opened after $28M Aspiration Fund endorsement deal raised cap circumvention concerns (NBA.com, ESPN)
- HIGH: Investigation expanded to include second endorsement deal with Daktronics — scoreboard/jumbotron manufacturer that supplied the video board at Clippers' Intuit Dome (NBC Sports, CBS Sports)
- HIGH: Allegation is Daktronics was used as vehicle to funnel money from Clippers to Leonard (CBS Sports)
- HIGH: Trade terms — Leonard to Toronto for Ingram, Dick, 2031+2033 unprotected 1sts, 2027 swap, 2 2nds (ESPN, NBA.com)
- MEDIUM: HoopsHype (Aug 10): resolution expected within six weeks, with sanctions expected against Clippers but trade expected to be cleared
- MEDIUM: Kawhi working under belief investigation will conclude before training camp (HoopsHype Aug 10)
- HIGH: Kawhi owed $50.3M in 2026-27 season
- MEDIUM: Commissioner Adam Silver publicly explained the league's investigation process (SI/All Clippers)
- MEDIUM: Toronto training camp Sept 28-29 in Quebec City
- HIGH: CBA does not allow player suspension for cap circumvention
**Story angle:** The Daktronics angle is the fresh news — a second suspicious deal involving a company that literally supplies equipment to the Clippers' own arena makes this investigation look more damaging to the Clippers organization.
